body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm tr}\), for every fixed \(K\) with a nonempty regular subclass, construct uniformly in \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\) a strictly positive boundary null \(P_{0,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a)\) with \(d(P_{0,a})=0\) and a legal transverse path \(P_{t,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a)\) for which \(d(P_{t,a})\ge c|t|\) and \(D_{\rm KL}(P_{t,a}\|P_{0,a})\le C t^2\), where \(c,C\) and the cell and link slack are uniform in \(a\). Does this yield \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c' n^{-1/2}\) uniformly in \(a\)?
body.justification: A root-\(n\) lower bound requires an actual regular boundary point and a legal path rather than finite-dimensional intuition.
body.gap: Neither the one-NCO testing result nor the inverse Gaussian comparators provide a uniformly legal transverse subexperiment inside this multinomial class.
body.consumer: Resolving the question determines whether the fixed-support upper rate is genuinely minimax sharp.
